title: The Chiefs Are Going To Be NFL Main Characters Again, Aren’t They?
contentHtml:
NFL fans who’d grown tired of the Kansas City Chiefs and their dominance — ushering them along the familiar path from loveable upstart to irritating juggernaut, like many other dynasties before them — got their wish last year.

Subscribe now

After seeing their run of close-game luck become irrelevant against the Eagles in Super Bowl LIX, the Chiefs then experienced a totally uncharacteristic run of bad luck on multiple fronts in 2025: Not only did their record swing back well past the point of standard regression-to-the-mean — they went from +4.9 wins per 17 over what their point differential would have predicted in 20241 to -3.5 per 17 last year,2 a record-smashing 8.4-win year-over-year luck swing — but they also lost Patrick Mahomes, arguably the best QB in the league,3 to a season-ending ACL tear in December.

All told, K.C. crash-landed to just 6 wins a year ago, their worst winning percentage since going 2-14 in 2012. But with apologies to rival fans who reveled in the Chiefs’ misery… it’s probably not going to last into 2026. Kansas City is poised to snap back to contention — even if not quite the same as when they were squeaking their way toward a Super Bowl date with Philadelphia.

The Chiefs’ arc is already one we’ve basically never seen before in NFL history — and that’s before we even consider what they’re trying to do as a return to glory in 2026. Going back again to the 1970 merger, no team cleared +2.5 wins per 17 relative to Pythagorean record in one season and was -2.5 wins or worse in the next.
